title: Milestone 1: Project & Git
subtitle: Build your first real app and push it to GitHub like a Pro.
goal: Combine strings, math, and inputs to build a calculator, then save it on GitHub.

blocks.heading: Welcome to the Pro leagues
blocks.html:
You've learned enough to build real things. Pros don't just learn syntax; they build projects and share them. Today, we step outside the browser.

You will build a Tip Calculator on your own computer and push it to GitHub.

blocks.heading: Step 1: Install Python
blocks.html: Go to python.org and install Python. Make sure to check the box that says 'Add Python to PATH'.

blocks.heading: Step 2: Get a Code Editor
blocks.html: Download VS Code. It's what the pros use. Install the Python extension inside it.

blocks.heading: Step 3: Build the Tip Calculator
blocks.html: Create a file named calculator.py. Write a program that asks for the bill amount, the tip percentage, and how many people are splitting it. Then, print out how much each person should pay.

blocks.caption: A hint for your calculator.py
blocks.code:
print("Welcome to the Tip Calculator!")
bill = float(input("What was the total bill? $"))
tip = int(input("How much tip would you like to give? 10, 12, or 15? "))
people = int(input("How many people to split the bill? "))
# Now do the math!

blocks.heading: Step 4: Push to GitHub
blocks.html:
Pros use Git to save their code. Create a GitHub account. Download GitHub Desktop for the easiest way to push code, or use the terminal:

git init
git add calculator.py
git commit -m "Initial commit"
git branch -M main
git remote add origin <your-repo-url>
git push -u origin main

blocks.question: Why do programmers use GitHub?
options: To save code, track changes, and share with others
To make their computer run faster
blocks.explain: GitHub is like Google Drive for code. It saves your work and lets you show it off.

challenge.title: Complete your GitHub push
challenge.instructions: There is no in-browser code challenge for this milestone! Your challenge is to build the Tip Calculator on your PC and push it to GitHub. Once it's live on GitHub, you've completed this milestone.
